title: Set a toilet's two closet bolts: T-heads down the flange slots, slid round to the floor line, retainers pushed down
instruction: Set both closet bolts: head down through each slot's wide end, slid round to the yellow line, retainer pushed down onto the ring.
context: Every toilet set or reset starts with the closet bolts. Each bolt's flat T-head goes down through the wide end of a slot in the floor flange's ring and is slid round under the ring until the two bolts stand on a line through the flange's centre parallel to the wall, where the holes in the toilet's base will come down over them. The head is out of sight under the ring, so the slide is felt, not seen. A plastic retainer washer is then pushed about 5 cm down each bolt's thread onto the ring so the bolt stands upright on its own and cannot slide back. Done by plumbers (O*NET 47-2152.00: "Install pipe assemblies, fittings, valves, appliances such as dishwashers or water heaters, or fixtures such as sinks or toilets, using hand or power tools.") and general maintenance and repair workers (49-9071.00).
setup: Millimetres from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the bench. 1) Floor: a 14 x 14 in (355.6) square of 23/32 in (18.3) plywood subfloor nailed to two 2x4s laid flat (38.1 x 88.9, 355.6 long) under its left and right edges, centred at (178, 0), its sides along x and y, clamped to the bench; its top is 56.4 above the bench. A 104 square hole under the flange takes its hub. 2) Flange: an Oatey 43495 3 x 4 in PVC closet flange with stainless-steel ring (fits over 3 in or inside 4 in pipe), centred at (180, 0), its ring screwed to the plywood with four 1 1/4 in flat-head wood screws. Ring (Oatey's drawing for its 3 or 4 in ring): 129 inside, 178 outside, 8.1 tall overall, top 8.1 above the floor, two closet-bolt slots on opposite sides. Slot sizes are estimates scaled from the drawing (check with a ruler): centre line 75 from the flange's centre, narrow part 7.5 wide, wide end 14 x 24, 53 end to end; the head's shelf 3.5 below the ring's underside (estimate). Turn the ring so the yellow line crosses each slot's narrow part 12 from its closed end: the right slot's wide end toward the robot, the left one's toward the wall. 3) Line: a 3 wide yellow lumber-crayon line on the plywood at x = 180 (through the flange's centre, parallel to the wall behind the toilet), from 93 to 150 each side of the centre. 4) Bolts: a Danco 88772A pair of 1/4-20 x 2 1/4 in yellow-zinc steel closet bolts (59.7 overall; flat T-head about 19 x 9.5 x 2.5, about 16 g each: estimates, check with a ruler and a kitchen scale), each with one of the pack's white plastic retainer washers (about 22 across, 2 thick, 1 g: estimates) pushed 2 onto its threaded tip by hand. Each stands on its head, upright, in the middle of a black rubber mat (70 x 70 x 3, fixed) centred at (110, -130) on the right and (110, 130) on the left, its head's length along (0.927, -0.375) on the right and (-0.927, 0.375) on the left. 5) Retainer grip (estimate; check: stand a bolt head-down on a kitchen scale and push the retainer down with a finger): it moves down the thread under about 3.5 N (2.5 N once moving). Frictions (estimates): steel on steel or PVC 0.3, retainer plastic 0.5, rubber 0.9, plywood 0.5. Start: both arms at their ready pose, grippers open. The README lists every collider, joint and mass.
scoring: Judged at the end of the run from the top-camera video, a photo and a ruler (in simulation from the poses). A bolt's head is in a slot when its shank stands in that slot (narrow part or wide end) with the head below the ring. A bolt is set when: its shank stands in its slot's narrow part with the shank's centre within 3 mm of the yellow line (lay a straightedge along both line marks); its retainer has been pushed down the thread until its underside is within 2 mm of the ring's top (a 2 mm card does not slide under it); the bolt is within 5 degrees of upright (its tip within 5 mm of a square stood beside it); no gripper is within 3 cm of it, and it has been still for 1 s. A slot is set when a set bolt stands in it. Score 0 if a bolt fell off the bench at any time, or if neither slot holds a bolt's head (doing nothing scores 0). Otherwise the lowest of these numbers that applies: 0.25 if neither slot is set; 0.5 if one slot is set and the other holds no bolt's head; 0.75 if one slot is set and the other is not; 1.0 when both slots are set. Either bolt may go in either slot.
reset_notes: About 2 minutes. Pull each retainer up off its bolt's thread (twist it as you pull), slide each bolt back to its slot's wide end and lift it out. Push a retainer 2 mm onto each bolt's tip by hand and stand each bolt on its head in the middle of its mat, the head's length as in the setup. Check the ring has not turned (the yellow line still crosses each slot 12 mm from its closed end). A retainer whose fingers no longer grip the thread (it slides down under its own weight) is replaced from a new Danco 88772A pack. Return both arms to the ready pose.
fidelity: Rigid bodies. The retainer's finger grip on the thread is a slide along the bolt that moves only past about 3.5 N (2.5 N sliding; estimate); the thread is a plain cylinder. Each retainer starts 2 mm onto its bolt's tip, as at reset, because that slide must exist from the start; it cannot come off the tip in simulation. The ring and slots are convex pieces at the published ring sizes; slot, head, shelf and retainer sizes, masses and frictions are estimates.
